title: Public measured datasets that constrain the Q100 vocal-fold model (inputs/Q100_model.py, inputs/Q100_QUESTION.md)
scope: Availability and identifiability only. No Q100 parameter was fitted, changed or validated here (PREREG.md N3).

criteria.C1: resolvable public URL fetched with HTTP 200 in this session
criteria.C2: licence stated by the record/landing page
criteria.C3: size stated from record metadata; any downloaded sample <= 52,428,800 B (50 MiB)
criteria.C4: measured (MRI/CT/HSV/pressure-flow/audio on tissue or speakers), not simulated
criteria.C5: names at least one Parameters field of inputs/Q100_model.py or one of the four declared outputs
criteria.C6: downloaded sample actually loaded here, with shape/dtype/units/coordinate frame printed by scripts/check_samples.py

sources.name: BAGLS - Benchmark for Automatic Glottis Segmentation
sources.paper: Gomez et al., BAGLS, a multihospital Benchmark for Automatic Glottis Segmentation, Scientific Data 7:186 (2020), https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0526-3
sources.format: PNG endoscopic frames + PNG binary glottis masks + JSON metadata (.meta) + mp4 raw videos; lossless PNG

subjects.health_status: 380 healthy, 262 identified disorder or clearly affected oscillation, 50 unknown

sources.measurement_nature: high-speed videoendoscopy of human vocal folds, expert-segmented glottal area per frame (ground truth, mean inter-expert IoU 0.772)

constrains.how: segmented glottal area per frame gives the open-area time series and its maximum, i.e. an empirical value for the rest/open area instead of the assumed 1.5e-5 m^2
minimum segmented area per cycle bounds the contact threshold area, assumed 1.64e-5 m^2
fraction of frames with area at/below the contact threshold is exactly the quantity the model reports as contact_percent; BAGLS supplies 55,750+3,500 labelled frames to measure it
frame rate is declared per frame in .meta, so f0 is computable from the mask time series
lateral wall excursion amplitude per frame bounds the lumped lateral masses, currently assumed 8e-4 and 6e-4 kg

sources.sample_method: HTTP Range into the 207,236,572 B test.zip: 4,000,000 B of tail for the zip central directory, then one image/mask/metadata triple, 4,028,979 B transferred in total (scripts/fetch_bagls_sample.py)
known_limits: areas are in px^2; the record gives no endoscope working distance, so px^2 cannot be converted to mm^2 from the record alone
sampling rate varies per recording (1000-10000 Hz) and must be read per frame from .meta
CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 forbids commercial use and requires share-alike
multi-hospital heterogeneity means a subject-matched comparison to one Q100 operating point is not possible

sources.name: Subglottal Pressure Experiments with Ex-vivo Porcine Larynges
sources.kind: parameters + time series (pressure, adduction, wall trajectories)
sources.creators: Birk, Semmler, Donhauser, Gomez, Schuetzenberger, Doellinger
sources.format: mp4 high-speed videoendoscopy + CSV metadata + numpy .npy trajectory array
sources.measurement_nature: measured subglottal pressure in Pa, arytenoid adduction torque in mNm, glottal-wall trajectories from expert segmentation (Glottis Analysis Tools); in this session the sample gave psub 459.1-1494.1 Pa over 288 rows

constrains.how: measured subglottal pressure per recording; Q100 freezes p_sub = 800 Pa as a 'protocol input' and the record shows measured values spanning roughly 460-1490 Pa, so the protocol value is inside the measured range but is not a subject-matched value
left/right glottal-wall trajectories at three longitudinal positions give the medial-surface displacement directly, which is what area0 and the projected width area_slope encode
sham gap 0 mm larynges provide recordings at/through contact, so the contact threshold and the contact duty can be measured rather than assumed
pressure-set recordings at known geometry allow a pressure-flow characteristic if the videos are re-segmented

sources.sample_method: direct file download from the record, 28,326,561 B; md5 of both files matches the record metadata
known_limits: ex-vivo porcine tissue: not human, no mucosal lubrication, no muscle activation
trajectories.npy declares no unit and no coordinate frame; magnitudes are O(10) and mm is plausible but unverified
frame rate of the source videos is not declared by the record

sources.name: Dynamic 3D MRI of vocal fold oscillations: thickness, contact area and glottal area waveform across phonation types
sources.creators: Traser, Stritt, Jordan, Koeberlein, Kirsch, Rummel, Zhang, Richter, Bock, Fischer, Echternach
sources.licence_source: Zenodo record metadata field license.id; record text also states CC BY 4.0 on acceptance
sources.format: NRRD volumes (raw double), binary STL surface reconstructions, WAV audio, MP4/GIF supplementary animations
sources.measurement_nature: dynamic 3-D ZTE MRI of the vibrating vocal folds with surface reconstruction, compared in the same record against simultaneous high-speed video, EGG and glottal area waveform

constrains.how: measured fold thickness per phonation type plus published tissue moduli is the only route to replacing the assumed 600 N/m and 1500 N/m layer springs with identified stiffnesses
3-D surface/volume per frame times tissue density bounds the lumped lateral masses (assumed 8e-4 / 6e-4 kg)
reconstructed medial surface gives the projected length/height that set the rest area and the projected-area derivative 3.0e-3 m
the record's own contact-area animations and GAW give contact duration per phonation type, the direct empirical counterpart of contact_percent
frame index to phase mapping plus the paired audio gives f0 for the same subject and phonation type

sources.sample_method: HTTP Range into the 5,228,064,118 B ZIP64 container: 200,000 B tail for the ZIP64 end-of-central-directory, one STL member read in full (1,405,684 B) and the first bytes of one 89,916,629 B NRRD member for its header; 840,639 B transferred (scripts/fetch_vf3d_members.py)
known_limits: n = 1 subject, so it constrains magnitudes, not a cohort distribution
10 phases per phonation type, not a dense oscillation time series
the NRRD header has no 'space units' field; mm is inferred from spacing 0.383929 and the file name token '08mm'
manuscript was submitted to JASA at the time of the record; peer review status not checked here

sources.name: Supplementary data for Ikuma et al., Development of parameters towards voice bifurcations
sources.kind: time series + cohort (human high-speed video, pathology)
sources.format: mp4 high-speed videoendoscopy, 2000 fps (Case1-3) and 4000 fps (Case4) as declared in the record

subjects.cases: no pathology; unilateral vocal fold paralysis (biphonia); polyp (biphonia + subharmonics); polyp (subharmonics + random)

sources.measurement_nature: laryngeal high-speed videoendoscopy of sustained /i/ phonation in healthy and pathological larynges

constrains.how: declared frame rate makes f0 measurable per case, including subharmonic and random vibration
pathological vibration types are the falsification cases for a contact law tuned on one healthy operating point
biphonia/subharmonic cases are where a unilateral contact law either holds or breaks, so they are the discriminating data for the contact stiffness

sources.sample_method: direct download of Case2.mp4, 202,005 B; md5 matches the record metadata
known_limits: DATA QUALITY: the record declares 2000 fps, but the parsed MP4 time base (media timescale 10240, stts sample delta 1792) gives 5.714 fps over 904 frames and 158.2 s; f0 must not be derived from this file without an independent timing source
no geometry, pressure or area is stored, so only kinematics can be extracted
four cases, single centre, no healthy cohort for comparison

sources.name: Ultrafast dynamic 3-D MRI of the vocal fold oscillation, phase II - representative pathology cases
sources.format: mp4 videolaryngostroboscopy, audio removed for data protection

subjects.cases: vocal fold polyp, muscle tension dysphonia, vocal fold scar, bilateral vocal fold nodules, vocal fold paresis

sources.measurement_nature: videolaryngostroboscopic recording of respiration and phonation per pathology

constrains.how: per-pathology phonation videos give f0 and its variability, the cohort test for a model calibrated at one operating point
organic and functional lesions are where measured contact behaviour departs most from a single contact stiffness

known_limits: total 72,124,458 B exceeds the 50 MiB single-sample budget although individual files fit; not downloaded because four samples were already verified
audio deliberately removed, so no acoustic reference

sources.name: Dresden Vocal Tract Dataset (DVTD)
sources.kind: geometry/anatomy (vocal tract, not vocal folds) + measured aeroacoustics
sources.paper: Birkholz et al., Printable 3D vocal tract shapes from MRI data and their acoustic and aerodynamic properties, Scientific Data (2020), https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-00597-w
sources.format: 3-D MRI vocal tract shapes, printable STL models, FEM models, measured and simulated aeroacoustic data
sources.measurement_nature: MRI of the vocal tract plus measured acoustic and aerodynamic response of 3-D printed replicas

constrains.how: only indirectly: measured tract length and the classic tract-length/f0 relation, i.e. a plausibility band for f0, not a vocal-fold constraint

known_limits: WEAKEST ENTRY: two speakers and no vocal fold at all; listed for completeness of the geometry category, it cannot identify any Q100 layer, contact or mucus parameter

rejected_or_not_found.candidate: VocalFold11b / Zheng et al. 3-D vocal fold geometry and CFD boundary conditions (M5 profile)
rejected_or_not_found.status: NOT FOUND as a public dataset record
rejected_or_not_found.reason: no public record with a resolvable file URL, licence and file sizes was found on Zenodo or figshare; the widely cited M5 geometry is an idealized published model, so it fails C4 (measured, not simulated)
rejected_or_not_found.consequence: the 3-D flow-based constraint on F_air remains uncovered by open data

rejected_or_not_found.reason: record returns 0 files and no licence field; nothing to fetch, nothing licensed
rejected_or_not_found.consequence: a 65-recording / 50-patient annotated set is referenced but not obtainable

rejected_or_not_found.candidate: Aichinger et al. 2016, database of 375 laryngeal high-speed videos with audio, 80 pathological + 40 non-pathological subjects (LREC 2016, aclanthology L16-1122)
rejected_or_not_found.reason: the paper is public but no public file URL was found for the database itself
rejected_or_not_found.consequence: the strongest published pathological/non-pathological HSV cohort with simultaneous audio is not open

rejected_or_not_found.candidate: public measured mucosal wave propagation speed, in vivo layer stiffness (E), layer thickness, meniscus/contact angle, mucus film rheology
rejected_or_not_found.reason: Zenodo API queries for 'mucosal wave vocal fold', 'vocal fold stiffness', 'hemilarynx experiment' and 'vocal fold surface tension' returned only journal articles and non-data records; the classic measured values (mucosal wave speed, zero-stress length, layer moduli) live in articles and on request, not in open datasets
rejected_or_not_found.consequence: DECISIVE for the Q100 hypothesis: k_body, k_surface, c_body, c_surface, meniscus_force, meniscus_length, sheet_tension, mucus_height stay assumption-only. Public measured data can constrain geometry, kinematics, glottal area, contact duty, f0 and subglottal pressure, but NOT the layered-tissue material law. A layered-vs-two-mass comparison therefore cannot be settled from public data alone; it needs a targeted ex vivo measurement campaign or a private dataset.

output_constrained: output: mucosal wave velocity [m/s] (kinematically via wall trajectories, not as a wave-speed measurement)
coverage_of_q100_parameters.note: mucosal wave velocity stays UNKNOWN as a measured quantity: DS-02 and DS-03 give wall motion, not a wave-speed measurement, and no open dataset was found that measures it
